events.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe

Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.

After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.

Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot condemned a “racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation” against the country’s Arab citizens, after the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, accused Arab parties of electoral fraud without evidence.

Netanyahu has repeatedly targeted Arab parties and Palestinian citizens of Israel after his party received a disappointing electoral showing, accusing them of manipulating the election and being linked to Hamas. Israeli electoral authorities have rejected these claims as not being backed by evidence.

Continue reading...

events.title: Iran says it targeted US military radar in Bahrain in retaliatory strike
events.summary:
First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.

“This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.”

Continue reading...

events.title: Boxer on death row in Iran vows ‘not to bow before oppression’ after winning rights prize
events.summary:
Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award

A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.

Continue reading...

events.title: World’s top court to rule if Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
events.summary:
International court of justice has never before found a state guilty of genocide, and ruling will have implications for case against Israel

The world’s top court will deliver a judgment this week on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, in a landmark case that will set a critical 21st-century benchmark for the gravest of all international crimes.

The closely watched judgment could become one of the most significant moments in international law since the end of the second world war.

Continue reading...

events.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile
events.summary:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising

Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.

Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.

Continue reading...

events.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir
events.summary:
From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.

The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi, and you can read an excerpt from the book here.)

Continue reading...

events.title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm
events.summary:
Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo

The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.

A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.

Continue reading...

events.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’
events.summary:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.

Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘Pull back the curtain’ on treatment of sexual assault victims in court, says UK government adviser
events.summary:
Professor urges ministers to use awareness triggered by Russell Brand conviction to examine use of rape myths in trials

The debate triggered by high-profile cases must “pull back the curtain” on the treatment of people making allegations of sexual offences in the criminal justice system in England and Wales, the government’s independent adviser on rape has told the Guardian.

Prof Katrin Hohl, who has advised the government in an overhaul of how rape is treated by police forces and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said the government should use the public awareness triggered by Russell Brand’s conviction for rape to examine the use of rape myths and jury direction in trials.

Continue reading...

events.title: Trident nuclear submarine concludes record underwater deployment
events.summary:
HMS Vengeance’s seven-month patrol prompts fears over slow pace of maintenance of ageing fleet and strain on crew

A Trident nuclear submarine has concluded a record seven-month deployment, returning to the Faslane naval base in Scotland where its crew was greeted by the defence secretary, Wes Streeting.

HMS Vengeance began its patrol on 12 April and spent 217 days submerged before returning on Sunday, having left the country when Keir Starmer was in Downing Street and Manchester United were third in the Premier League.

Continue reading...

events.title: Labour rebellion over Rosebank oilfield expected to top 100 MPs
events.summary:
Total of 75 have already signed letter to Burnham opposing plans as discontent also grows over Europe and welfare changes

As many as 100 Labour MPs could sign a letter opposing the giant Rosebank oilfield, as discontent among backbenchers looks likely to surge this week, with rebellions also brewing over Europe and welfare changes.

A total of 75 MPs have already signed the private letter, which is expected to be delivered in the next fortnight to Andy Burnham as part of a campaign in which Labour MPs from the party’s 2024 intake are playing a significant role.

Continue reading...

events.title: Burnham pledges early intervention and ‘benefits backstop’ to tackle youth jobs crisis
events.summary:
Prime minister promises ‘root-and-branch rethink’ of support for young people as Milburn report advises sweeping changes to some benefits

  • Andy Burnham: The crisis facing Britain’s young people is politicians’ fault. To fix it, we need a generational response

Andy Burnham has pledged to intervene as early as childhood to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”.

Burnham said the government would intervene at all the stages of life in which young people fell behind, and “long before they find themselves out of work and reliant on the state”, including providing more opportunities for vocational training in schools.

Continue reading...

events.title: Planned asylum seeker detention centre next to Oxfordshire sewage works criticised
events.summary:
Thames Water says detainees at proposed accommodation should expect to experience insect swarms and strong smells

A Home Office plan to build asylum seeker detention facilities next to a sewage pump is facing objections after water company officials warned that detainees should expect to experience insect swarms and strong smells.

Proposed secure accommodation blocks at Campsfield House immigration removal centre in Oxfordshire will be 20 metres from a sewage pumping station, according to a written submission from Thames Water.

Continue reading...

events.title: Somali-American Uber driver brutally assaulted in alleged hate crime in Minnesota
events.summary:
Mohamed Yusuf is fighting for his life after alleged attack by passenger who said he did not like driver’s first name

A Somali-American Uber driver was allegedly brutally assaulted by a passenger in Hopkins, Minnesota, on Saturday, in what his family says “appears to be a hate crime”.

The driver, Mohamed Yusuf, is currently hospitalized and fighting for his life, his family told the Somali Brief, a digital news site run by two Somali American journalists. The driver’s cousin, Abdinasir Ali told the outlet that the alleged attack took place early Saturday after a passenger in Hopkins, a suburban city south-west of Minneapolis, asked Yusuf’s name and then said he did not like the name Mohamed.

Continue reading...

events.title: LSU star MiLaysia Fulwiley arrested after allegedly striking police officer with car
events.summary:
• Guard allegedly tried to flee traffic stop in Baton Rouge

  • Tigers say they are aware of situation involving player

LSU guard MiLaysia Fulwiley, one of the ninth-ranked Tigers’ leading scorers, was arrested after allegedly striking a police officer while attempting to flee from a traffic stop.

LSU’s athletic department, in a written statement provided to The Associated Press, said university officials “are aware of the situation and have no further comment at this time as it’s an ongoing legal matter.”

Continue reading...

events.title: Texas puts to death man who beheaded three children, hours after Oklahoma execution
events.summary:
Oklahoma man, 73, executed for killing ex’s estranged husband, as US nears 40 executions for second straight year

A Texas man convicted of fatally stabbing and beheading his three young children in a squalid, windowless apartment in 2003 was recently executed.

John Allen Rubio, 46, was pronounced dead at 6.47 pm on Thursday after a lethal injection at the state prison in Huntsville, Texas. His killings of his baby girl and two toddlers so rocked the city of Brownsville on the US border with Mexico that the apartment building was later demolished – and the land turned into a park and community garden.

Continue reading...

events.title: Senator-elect Scott Colom vows to ensure Trump follows through on his promises
events.summary:
Mississippi Democrat points to commitments Trump made: lower prices, halt endless wars and release Epstein files

After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Donald Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024.

Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.

Continue reading...

events.title: Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer
events.summary:
Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers

Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer, asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances.

Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.

events.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people gathered to protest against the government's plan to abolish broadcasting fees. Critics say the nationalist coalition would like to secure control over the media.

events.summary: The majority of the migrants who arrived on the islands on Saturday came from Senegal, Gambia, and Guinea. The surge in arrivals to the Canaries comes after Spain's Ceuta recently faced a migration crisis.

events.summary: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

events.summary: Southeast Asian leaders have agreed to engage Myanmar in stages after years of excluding its leaders from high-level meetings. The bloc says Myanmar could regain full representation if it makes progress on a peace plan.

events.summary: The scale of the economic disruption caused by AI has led even conservative politicians to talk about universal basic income. But economists aren't convinced, and campaigners think we need to ask deeper questions.

events.summary: Some 106,000 people marched through French cities for a fifth consecutive weekend of protests, marking the lowest turnout in recent weeks.

events.summary: Eleven countries took part in the competition in Bangkok. Teenage winner Carmelle Collado's winning dance song is a tribute to Filipino women.

events.summary: The successful recovery of SpaceX's Starship marks a breakthrough in founder Elon Musk's goal of developing a fully reusable rocket system.

events.summary: The 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?

events.summary: As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 polls, the use of artificial intelligence in the electoral process has prompted questions about integrity and institutional readiness. Can Nigerians trust their democratic processes?

events.summary: South Sudan has been independent from Sudan since 2011, and has not yet held national elections. Since then, the country faces cycles of violence after a civil war led to a tenuous peace deal.

events.title: US: Duffy says 'incompetence' or bad tech to blame for flight haltings
events.summary: Air carriers in the US canceled some 16,000 flights over the past 24 hours in the biggest such grounding since 9/11. Officials hinted that incompetence or faulty equipment, not malfeasance, is the cause.

events.title: Werner Holzer Prize awarded to Katja Gloger and DW's Jaafar Abdul Karim
events.summary: DW journalist Jaafar Abdul Karim and Russia correspondent Katja Gloger have been awarded the prestigious Werner Holzer Prize for international journalism.

events.summary: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

events.summary: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, addressed via his songs and sharp wit. At 90, he's as feisty as ever.

events.summary: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

events.title: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
events.summary: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

events.summary: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

events.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
events.summary: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

events.title: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany
events.summary: Two weeks after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

events.title: Germany gives sweeping powers to police, intelligence services
events.summary: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?

events.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
events.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms has cast doubt on Anthropic's looming IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

events.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
events.summary: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

events.title: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget
events.summary: The budget committee in the Bundestag worked into the night to sign off on next year's spending plans. These include levels of new debt only eclipsed once, at the height of the COVID pandemic. DW has more.

events.title: Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
events.summary: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.

events.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
events.summary: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.

events.summary: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

events.title: Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
events.summary: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

events.summary: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

events.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.

events.title: What are fossil fuels?
events.summary: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

events.title: Germany news: Police raid chapters of Gremium MC biker gang
events.summary: Police in southwestern Germany launched major early-morning operations against a biker gang. The state of Baden-Württemberg is outlawing three of its chapters. Meanwhile, unions are planning more strikes.

events.title: Bundeswehr study exposes widespread sexual harassment in German military
events.summary: Sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known, with younger women disproportionately affected. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has called for a policy of "zero tolerance."

events.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
events.summary: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

events.title: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe
events.summary: Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny commemorates the victims of Auschwitz as Jewish communities across Europe face growing hostility. What does the promise of "Never Again" mean for Jewish life in Europe today?

events.title: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge
events.summary: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

events.title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
events.summary: The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

events.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
events.summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

events.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
events.summary: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

events.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
events.summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

events.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
events.summary: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

events.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
events.summary: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

events.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
events.summary: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

events.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
events.summary: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

events.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
events.summary: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

events.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
events.summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

events.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
events.summary: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

events.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
events.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

events.summary: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

events.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
events.summary: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

events.summary: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

events.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
events.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

events.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
events.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

events.title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
events.summary: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

events.title: Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
events.summary: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

events.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
events.summary: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

events.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?

events.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
events.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

events.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

events.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

events.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
events.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

events.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
events.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

events.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
events.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

events.title: Kroupi on target as France beat Turkey to reach Nations League quarters
events.summary: Eli Junior Kroupi scored his maiden goal for France as Les Bleus beat Turkey 2-1 in Bordeaux on Sunday to top their group with 13 points and qualify for the quarter-finals of the Nations League. World Cup winners Spain, who lost at home against England, are among their potential opponents in the last eight.

events.title: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands in two days
events.summary: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached the Canary Islands over the past two days, Spain’s coastguard said Sunday, continuing a recent surge of arrivals from West African countries to the Spanish archipelago, where the authorities declared a migration emergency earlier this week.

events.title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
events.summary: Houthi forces in Yemen have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government, military and government sources said Sunday. The embattled government earlier announced it was pulling back its last forces from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend its temporary capital on the southern coast of Yemen.

events.title: Pragues's fight for public TV - Why Renowned Presenter Will Leave Czech TV Over Reforms
events.summary: Daniel Stach, one of the Czech Republic’s best-known television presenters, tells Gavin Lee on France 24 why he is prepared to walk away from his career rather than work under changes that he says will threaten the independence of public broadcasting. As hundreds of thousands take to the streets of Prague, Stach explains why he is joining the protests against the government’s proposed overhaul of public media funding – and what is at stake for Czech television, journalism and democracy.

events.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after 'sabotage' attempt at drone factory
events.summary: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its ​foreign minister ‌said on Sunday, following a suspected ⁠sabotage attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blamed on ‌Moscow.

events.title: How did over 2,000 migrants reach the Canaries in just 48 hours?
events.summary: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The strip of the Atlantic Ocean between West Africa and the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration routes – and the journey is usually made with ill-equipped dinghies and overcrowded boats. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Madrid, Sarah Morris.

events.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
events.summary: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

events.title: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships across country in midterm elections
events.summary: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor. She discusses the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children. “There was a realisation across the map that perhaps moms were the best messenger for this,” she explains, pointing to voters' concerns about “the cost of living, affordability, how to make ends meet.”

events.title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
events.summary: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

events.title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
events.summary: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

events.title: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
events.summary: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days time, and will meet President Putin and President Xi. There's likely to be one fewer tech giants at the table, Jensen Huang, newly resigned from Nvidia, over the suspected spy affair.

events.title: Santa school in full swing in London ahead of Christmas celebrations
events.summary: It may still be November but it's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in South London, as many Santa impersonators are heading to school for their festive training. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves, and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring the magic of Christmas to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

events.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
events.summary: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

events.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
events.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

events.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
events.summary: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

events.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
events.summary: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.

events.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly

events.title: French Ciryl Gane retains MMA heavyweaight title agianst Josh Hokit

Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with ​sporadic attacks continuing. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Bangkok Tommy Walker.

events.title: Will Ukraine make territorial concessions for NATO membership?
events.summary: The United States suggested Ukraine make territorial concessions in exchange for a NATO membership, according to Volodymyr Zelensky. events.summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.

events.title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
events.summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.

events.title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
events.summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.

events.title: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
events.summary: “Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” the country’s main unions said. “Anger is immense.”

events.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
events.summary: Six women alleged that the British comedian had sexually assaulted them at his home, in hotels and public bathrooms. Brand has denied all claims.

events.title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Russia-Ukraine peace as she hosts top officials at the White House
events.summary: Ukraine has been reeling from the worst collapse in relations with Washington since the start of the war.

events.title: U.S. Marine dies in Japan during training, military says
events.summary: The person, who has yet to be named, died Tuesday in Okinawa, the 3rd Marine Division said.
